**How to edit this file**

- Change only the text underneath a `###` heading. That text is what the game
  says.
- Leave the `##` headings, the `<!-- key: ... -->` comments and the `###`
  field names alone. They are how the text finds its way home.
- Keep any `%s` and `%d` exactly as they are. The game fills them in with a
  name or a level, and a line that loses one will break.
- Blank lines inside a passage are kept. Leading and trailing ones are not.
- Speaker names are part of the line ("Elder: Good morning."). The dialogue
  box splits them off itself, so keep the `Name: ` prefix.

## INNKEEPER — Town

<!-- key: scene:town.tscn:Actors/Innkeeper -->

<sub>game/areas/town.tscn · `Actors/Innkeeper`</sub>

### display_name

INNKEEPER

### dialogue_line

<!-- speaker: Innkeeper -->

Welcome to the Hearthside. Beds are warm and the stew is hot. Stay the night? Oathkeepers sleep free.

### chatter[0]

<!-- speaker: Innkeeper -->

Back again? Your Oathbound look like they could use a proper bed.

### chatter[1]

<!-- speaker: Innkeeper -->

The Fisher swears he caught tonight's stew. He didn't. Rest a while?

### barks[0]

Stew's on!

### barks[1]

Rooms free tonight!

### barks[2]

Wipe your boots, please.

## SCRIBE — Town

<!-- key: scene:town.tscn:Actors/Scribe -->

<sub>game/areas/town.tscn · `Actors/Scribe`</sub>

### display_name

SCRIBE

### dialogue_line

<!-- speaker: Scribe -->

Binding Scrolls, inked by my own hand. Oath-script holds better than any rope. It is the same hand that copies out the rite, for whatever that is worth to you.

### chatter[0]

<!-- speaker: Scribe -->

A worn-down creature listens closer. Weaken it before you offer the scroll.

### chatter[1]

<!-- speaker: Scribe -->

Failed binding? The scroll crumbles, but the lesson stays. Buy another.

### barks[0]

Scrolls! Fresh-inked scrolls!

### barks[1]

Bind your next friend!

### shop_title

Scribe's Stall

## APOTHECARY — Town

<!-- key: scene:town.tscn:Actors/Apothecary -->

<sub>game/areas/town.tscn · `Actors/Apothecary`</sub>

### display_name

APOTHECARY

### dialogue_line

<!-- speaker: Apothecary -->

Salves for scrapes, tonics for worse, and a draught for when the worst has already happened. I have stocked every champion since I was young.

### chatter[0]

<!-- speaker: Apothecary -->

Clearwater from the well, blessed twice. Burns and poisons don't stand a chance.

### chatter[1]

<!-- speaker: Apothecary -->

Keep a salve in your satchel. The meadow bites harder than it looks.

### barks[0]

Salves and tonics!

### barks[1]

Mind your wounds, traveller.

### shop_title

Apothecary

## GUARD — Town

<!-- key: scene:town.tscn:Actors/Guard -->

<sub>game/areas/town.tscn · `Actors/Guard`</sub>

### display_name

GUARD

### dialogue_line

<!-- speaker: Guard -->

The gate stays open while the sun is up. After dark, knock twice and say your oath. We have kept that rule since before the altar was raised.

### chatter[0]

<!-- speaker: Guard -->

Wild ones don't come past the wall. Mostly. Nothing has ever come past the altar.

### barks[0]

Quiet day.

### barks[1]

Mind the ruins out there.

## OLD MAN — Town

<!-- key: scene:town.tscn:Actors/OldMan -->

<sub>game/areas/town.tscn · `Actors/OldMan`</sub>

### display_name

OLD MAN

### dialogue_line

<!-- speaker: Old Man -->

The dead king has been put back under nine times since this town started keeping count, and the count was already old when we started it.

### chatter[0]

<!-- speaker: Old Man -->

Sit a while. Well water tastes better when you're not rushing, and that altar has waited longer than you have.

### barks[0]

Hmph. Pigeons.

### barks[1]

Back in my day...

## BARD — Town

<!-- key: scene:town.tscn:Actors/Bard -->

<sub>game/areas/town.tscn · `Actors/Bard`</sub>

### display_name

BARD

### dialogue_line

<!-- speaker: Bard -->

I'm writing a ballad about the Oathbreaker. Hardest song in the Reach. Nobody can agree on whether it is meant to end sad.

### chatter[0]

<!-- speaker: Bard -->

Every oath has a verse. Yours hasn't been written yet, and his has been sung wrong for a hundred years.

### barks[0]

♪ Oh, the meadow grass was green... ♪

### barks[1]

♪ ...and the scroll held true ♪
